standard_prerequisites.name: Sections of a sheaf over the empty open set form a singleton, per the remark on the empty sheaf convention
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives F(i^{-1}(U)) = {*} for neighbourhoods U of x disjoint from Z.

core_obligations: If x not in Z, X being a topological space with closed Z provides arbitrarily small neighbourhoods U of x with U intersect Z empty (proof lines 5176-5178); then i^{-1}(U) is empty and F(i^{-1}(U)) = {*} by the sheaf convention, so the stalk i_*F_x is a singleton (proof lines 5179-5181). If z in Z, every open neighbourhood of z in Z has the form Z cap U for U open in X, and the directed system of these agrees with the system of neighbourhoods of z in Z, so the stalk is F_z (proof lines 5181-5184). The canonical map i^{-1}i_*F -> F is an isomorphism on every stalk by the two cases just proven, hence an isomorphism of sheaves (proof lines 5184-5187). For abelian sheaves and sheaves of algebraic structures the same arguments apply with {*} replaced by 0 or the final object (proof lines 5189-5191).
proof_roadmap: Compute the stalk at x outside Z via disjoint neighbourhoods and the empty-set convention (proof lines 5176-5181).
Compute the stalk at z in Z via neighbourhoods of the form Z cap U and conclude the counit is a stalkwise isomorphism (proof lines 5181-5187).
